title: Round contract
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape Turing machine with state set $S$, anchor state $a$, escape set $E\subseteq \{\mathrm{None}\}\cup\{\mathrm{Some}(s):s\in S\}$, index type $I$, and fixed input $x$. A round contract consists of a precondition, a time, an endpoint configuration, and lower and upper integer bounds for each work-tape head, all depending on an index and a starting configuration. Whenever a starting configuration is in state $a$ and satisfies the precondition, its time is positive, the machine reaches the specified endpoint after exactly that many steps, and the endpoint state is either $a$ or an element of $E$. At every positive time strictly before the endpoint, the machine's state is neither halted nor in the anchor-or-escape stopping set; at every time up to and including the endpoint, each work-tape head position lies between its specified lower and upper bounds, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $k$ of work tapes
A symbol alphabet and state set
An escape set $E$ of optional states
Precondition, time, endpoint, and integer lower and upper bound functions
For every indexed starting configuration in state $a$ satisfying the precondition, the time is positive
The computation reaches the specified endpoint at exactly that time
The endpoint state is the anchor or belongs to the escape set
At each positive intermediate time strictly before the endpoint, the state is outside the round stopping set
For every work tape and every time up to and including the endpoint, the head position lies in the inclusive specified bounds
